deep.reconstruction:
Context: this folio is an early draft of §1 ('Eigenschaften der rationalen Zahlen') of Dedekind's 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872). The previous page dates the core idea to 24 Nov 1858 and names Heine's 'Elemente der Functionenlehre' (1872) as the trigger for writing, so the draft is from about 1872. It continues property II (density) from the previous page.

(II, continued) For distinct rationals a < c there are infinitely many rationals b with a < b < c. The collection of these b, including a and c (inserted above the line), may be written (a,c) = {b in Q : a <= b <= c}. If a, or c, or both are to be excluded, he writes (ā,c) = {a < b <= c}, (a,c̄) = {a <= b < c} and (ā,c̄) = {a < b < c}. A bar over an endpoint means that endpoint is excluded.

III (definition). A system R ⊆ Q is called an 'Intervall' if whenever a, c ∈ R, every rational between a and c also lies in R. In modern terms R is order-convex.

(Remark; the numeral here is struck.) Every system (a,c) is an interval. So is Q itself.

If every number of interval R also lies in interval S (R ⊆ S), then R is called a 'Stück' (piece) of S, contained in S.

IV (image reads IV). Every rational a splits Q into two pieces (−∞,a) and (a,+∞).
- The first contains all a1 < a.
- The second contains all a2 > a.
- a itself may be assigned to either piece.
- Every a2 is greater than every a1.

The implicit justification (mine) is transitivity from I: a1 < a < a2 implies a1 < a2. Both pieces are intervals, by transitivity again (mine).

Marginal note: the pieces or classes are to be denoted A1 and A2. This is exactly the notation of property III in the printed §1, where every rational a produces a partition of Q into classes A1, A2 with every a1 < every a2. This is the template later generalized to the Schnitt (A1, A2).
errors: Minor notational inconsistency: under his own convention (endpoints included unless barred), the first piece, containing all a1 < a, should be written (−∞,ā) and the second (ā,+∞). He writes (−∞,a) and (a,+∞), then says a may go to either piece. This is harmless but loose.
Infinite endpoints ±∞ are used in the interval symbol without the convention being stated.
No mathematical errors otherwise. The ordering facts are justified implicitly by transitivity (property I).

results.what: Notation for closed, half-open and open intervals of rationals using bars over excluded endpoints
Definition of an 'Intervall' as a subset of Q closed under betweenness
results.modern_name: order-convex set (interval in a linear order)
results.usually_credited_to: standard order theory (Cantor, Hausdorff era formalization)

results.what: Each rational a partitions Q into lower and upper classes A1, A2 with every a1 < every a2; a may be assigned to either class
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind, Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen (1872), §1 property III

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the published §1 of 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen', so the content is well known as Dedekind's. The only unpublished detail is the explicit definition of an order-convex 'Intervall' and the 'Stück' relation, which were dropped from the printed text. That is a minor insight into how the cut concept was framed, not a new result.

checkable.sympy: a, c = symbols('a c', rational=True); simplify(((a+c)/2 - a) - (c-a)/2) == 0
checkable.asserts: The midpoint of a and c exceeds a by (c-a)/2 > 0 when c > a, so a rational lies strictly between a and c (density, property II).
Example of the 'Stück' relation: (0,1) is a piece of (-1,2).

checkable.sympy: Intersection(Interval(-oo, Rational(1,2), right_open=True), Interval(Rational(1,2), oo, left_open=True)) == EmptySet
checkable.asserts: With a assigned to neither side, the lower piece {x < a} and upper piece {x > a} are disjoint (here a = 1/2).

checkable.sympy: Union(Interval(-oo, Rational(1,2)), Interval(Rational(1,2), oo, left_open=True)) == Interval(-oo, oo)
checkable.asserts: With a assigned to the lower class, A1 ∪ A2 covers the whole line (illustrating the split of the domain).

transcription_corrections: The numeral before 'Jede rationale Zahl a zerlegt das Gebiet…' reads 'IV.' in the image, not 'V.'
The struck numeral before 'Jedes System (a,c) z. B. bildet ein Intervall' appears simply deleted. No replacement numeral 'IV' is clearly visible, so that sentence is an unnumbered remark.
The struck word before 'soll a, oder c' is illegible. 'Gleichfalls[?]' is doubtful; it could be 'Nöthigenfalls' or similar.
